metadata.description: pablolok's Claude Code skills — one plugin per skill.

plugins.name: backlog
plugins.description: Manage a project's tracked work in BACKLOG.md — add, list, process, close; AND the entry point when STARTING work that needs a design doc (spec, plan, report) — open a BKLG entry first, unasked, so its doc folder is tracked and archived. Ships the doc gates, a GitHub Issues mirror and a local dashboard. Trigger on "/backlog", "add to backlog", "metti nel backlog", "what's in the backlog", "backlog dashboard", "close BKLG-NNN", or before creating a features/bugs/diagnostic/analysis folder.

plugins.name: clean-code-standards
plugins.description: A language-agnostic clean-code / OOP quality bar. Use whenever writing, refactoring, or reviewing code in ANY language — enforces single-responsibility, injected collaborators, Tell-Don't-Ask, no god objects, no business logic in static/global scope, strong typing over magic values, centralized literals, a reuse audit, fail-fast inputs, and no warning suppression. This is the universal core; per-language skills (e.g. csharp-oop-standards) layer their own idioms on top of it.

plugins.name: csharp-oop-standards
plugins.description: The C#-specific layer on top of clean-code-standards. Use whenever writing, refactoring, or reviewing C#. Assumes the language-agnostic core (SRP, injected collaborators, Tell-Don't-Ask, no god objects, no static business logic, strong typing, literal centralization, reuse audit, fail-fast, no warning suppression) and adds only the C#/.NET idioms, tooling, and coverage bar. The persistence conventions (repository/UnitOfWork/EF Core) apply only to a project that uses EF Core.

plugins.name: diff-self-review
plugins.description: Use before every commit and before declaring work done, and when accepting another agent's diff — read the REAL diff (staged, unstaged, untracked) and trace every hunk to the stated ask, so nothing changes behaviour that nobody asked for. Catches changed defaults, signatures, error text, ordering, conditions, swallowed errors, drive-by refactors and leftovers; each is reverted or declared in the hand-back. Intent tracing, not a bug hunt; verification-gates owns the gates and removals.

plugins.name: jira-workflow
plugins.description: Use whenever work is tracked in Jira — before touching code, at every step, on a status change, commit or release, and when creating tickets, logging time or linking dependencies through the Atlassian connector. Tracker first, status moved when the fact happens, points and hours on every ticket, continuous worklogs, Blocks links in the right direction, the total review queries and the connector's pitfalls. Statuses, labels, sprints and field ids come from the project's playbook.

plugins.name: mermaid-diagrams
plugins.description: Mermaid diagrams in the markdown docs of ANY project, so that they really RENDER in the VS Code preview and on GitHub. Use it before adding or changing a diagram in docs/ — layers, architecture, UML, sequence. Carries the rule for when to pre-render to SVG, the validator and the renderer behind one stable project command, the mechanism by which the preview leaves empty boxes with no error, and the dead ends already ruled out.

plugins.name: pre-implementation-review
plugins.description: Use BEFORE writing code, patching files, or scaffolding UI/backend changes — decide the RIGHT design first (responsibilities, the design pattern that expresses each, ownership, seams); reuse, testability and low duplication then follow as consequences. Trigger during reasoning and planning, especially when a change introduces new responsibilities, collaborators, shared services, UI patterns, validators, or orchestration logic. This is the "plan clean" front-half of clean-code-standards.

plugins.name: python-standards
plugins.description: The Python-specific layer on top of clean-code-standards. Use whenever writing, refactoring, or reviewing Python — scripts, packages, services, tests. Assumes the language-agnostic core and adds only the Python idioms — injection without import-time side effects, type hints with Protocol/Enum/dataclass, narrow exceptions, no mutable defaults, pathlib and explicit encodings, safe subprocess, logging, and the project's own runner, minimum version and checkers — never tools it does not use.

plugins.name: review-backlog
plugins.description: Periodic review of a project's backlog (the backlog skill's BACKLOG.md) — run the document gates, clean up what has rotted, and close with ONE proposal of what to do next. Use when the user says "review the backlog", "what's next", "review del backlog", "cosa facciamo adesso", "controlla che i documenti siano a posto", or at the start of a session with no work in progress. Read-only until the cleanup, and the cleanup touches ONLY documents.

plugins.name: savvy-flow
plugins.description: Orchestrated delivery flow. The session model plans, owns design, delegates implementation to tiered worker subagents (savvy-fable / savvy-heavy / savvy-careful / savvy-medium / savvy-light) and adversarially reviews their output. Invoke with /savvy-flow <task>.

plugins.name: savvy-progress
plugins.description: Progress bar above the prompt for /savvy-flow, plus an agents panel (/agents-info): running, finished and planned subagents with model, task progress, context, cost and time.

plugins.name: skill-retrospective
plugins.description: Use when a piece of work closes — a backlog entry archived, a tracked parent ticket or piece of work closed, a multi-round loop ended, a deliverable accepted or rejected, the user correcting the method; the close steps of backlog and jira-workflow invoke it, and a hook asks after an archive or a run of commits. Reviews what the work taught and rewrites the skills it used in place so the next run is shorter and right first time; never appends a lessons log.

plugins.name: test-design-standards
plugins.description: What a good test is made of, in any language. Use whenever writing, changing or reviewing tests — a bug fixed from a test that reproduces it, behaviour through the public seam, one behaviour per test, deterministic and isolated (no clock, sleep, run order or shared state), doubles only for what the unit does not own, every state and error path, the right level, timing tests run alone, flaky tests fixed or quarantined, never silenced. Layers on clean-code-standards; not the TDD loop.

plugins.name: typescript-react-standards
plugins.description: The TypeScript/React-specific layer on top of clean-code-standards. Use whenever writing, refactoring, or reviewing TypeScript, React, or Node/Deno code. Assumes the language-agnostic core of clean-code-standards and adds only the TS/React idioms, tooling, and quality gates.

plugins.name: verification-gates
plugins.description: Use before declaring code work done / handing it back — verify that the required automated gates are green across any stack (tests, builds, compilers, bundlers, linters, static analysis) and that nothing was silently removed. Applies to changed code in any language. Confirms green evidence rather than assuming it; who RUNS the gates depends on the project (some environments have the user run them). This is the "verify clean" back-half of clean-code-standards.

plugins.name: writing-architecture-docs
plugins.description: Use when a piece of work must be designed before it is written — a large feature, a rework, a defect that crosses several layers, a multi-phase job — or when the question is "how is it built today", "what shape must it take", "why this and not something else". Any project, any language. The diagram mechanics are NOT here — they are in the mermaid-diagrams skill.
